assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new therapeutic modality built on chemically induced proximity: bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues hijack E3 ligases to degrade targets previously considered undruggable. Conceptually original and clinically consequential, with strong appeal from a molecular-design and translational perspective.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and validated the PROTAC concept; Ciulli provided structure-guided VHL-based design that made degraders drug-like. The thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, others) is a separate contribution and fits awkwardly into three names.
assessment.maturity: Many candidates are in clinical trials and mechanisms are well confirmed, but approval of a degrader drug is still pending; timing is somewhat early yet defensible.
uncertainties: Whether molecular glues and PROTACs should be recognized together or separately
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli and the cereblon discoverers
Clinical impact not yet fully demonstrated

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs let cells incorporate designed noncanonical amino acids, a general platform for protein engineering, biophysics, bioorthogonal labeling and biotherapeutics. Highly original and transformative for chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first in vivo incorporation of unnatural amino acids in cells; Chin extended it to multicellular organisms, quadruplet codons and genome recoding. Mehl and Yokoyama are also important, so the three-name limit forces exclusions.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent adoption and broad use; the field is mature and stable.
uncertainties: Choice among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama
Overlap with the earlier Nobel-recognized directed evolution and phage display fields is modest

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation enables chemoselective joining of unprotected peptides, making total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins routine, including modified proteins and designed peptide constructs. A foundational enabling chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Dawson and Kent introduced native chemical ligation; Muir developed expressed protein ligation and semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu contributed important extensions, so credit is broad.
assessment.maturity: Well established for about 30 years and widely reproduced; recognition would be timely or even overdue.
uncertainties: Exact core trio given Danishefsky's role in related ligation chemistry
Practical limits for very large proteins

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the delivery chemistry that makes siRNA and mRNA medicines work, with enormous demonstrated societal impact including COVID-19 vaccines. Combines lipid self-assembly with biological function; strongly translational.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues developed ionizable lipid and nanoparticle formulation principles; Langer and Anderson pioneered combinatorial lipidoid libraries. Contributions of many industry and academic scientists are intertwined and credit is difficult to bound.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale, so recognition is timely, although the mRNA vaccine prize in Medicine 2023 may reduce appetite.
uncertainties: Whether this is judged chemistry rather than pharmaceutical formulation

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA origami demonstrated programmable folding of long DNA into arbitrary nanoscale shapes, enabling nanoscale templating, plasmonic and biosensing platforms and drug carriers. Original and visually striking, with a wide user base.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund is the clear inventor of scaffolded DNA origami; Shih and Yan were prominent in extending it to 3D and applications. Seeman's earlier structural DNA nanotechnology is not on the credited list, which complicates fair attribution.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a method, but real-world applications beyond research tools are still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle for membraneless compartments in cells changed how molecular assembly and function are viewed, linking physical chemistry of polymers and peptides to cell biology.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne started the field with P granules; Rosen showed multivalent interactions drive phase separation. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical-chemical grounding.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing but still debated: physiological relevance and specificity of condensates in vivo remain contested, so maturity is moderate.
uncertainties: Controversy over in vivo relevance versus in vitro droplets
Fit with chemistry versus physiology prizes

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly and spherical nucleic acids link molecular recognition to nanomaterials, underpinning colorimetric biosensing, diagnostics and intracellular gene regulation. Directly relevant to peptide/DNA-nanoparticle bioassays.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin and Alivisatos independently reported DNA-directed gold nanoparticle assembly in 1996; Mirkin's spherical nucleic acid work was the main continuing effort. Storhoff and Mucic were trainee/coauthors.
assessment.maturity: Established for decades with commercial diagnostics, though therapeutic translation has been limited.
uncertainties: Close competition with other nanomaterials candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native mass spectrometry measures intact noncovalent protein complexes, stoichiometry and membrane protein-lipid interactions, a complement to structural biology and biophysical characterization.
assessment.attribution: Robinson is central for native MS of large complexes and membrane proteins; Heck and Chait developed methods and applications widely. Loo and Gross contributed foundational ESI work; Fenn and Tanaka were already recognized for ionization.
assessment.maturity: Mature with broad adoption and expanding use; recognition could be timely.
uncertainties: Relationship to the 2002 mass spectrometry prize
Crowded analytical chemistry field with other MS candidates
